name: multi-cloud
context: Distributed workloads across multiple independent cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) to avoid vendor lock-in, improve resilience, and optimize costs through strategic workload placement
benefits: Vendor lock-in avoidance through provider independence
Best-of-breed service selection from each provider
Resilience against provider outages with automatic failover
Regulatory compliance via data residency control
Elastic capacity bursting across providers during demand spikes
Geographic distribution with regional service proximity
M&A flexibility to absorb companies on different clouds
tradeoffs: Operational complexity with multiple platforms to manage
Networking complexity requiring careful IP planning
Data consistency challenges across distributed systems
Skill requirements for multiple cloud platforms
use_cases: Enterprise procurement requiring competitive sourcing across providers
Regulatory data residency requirements for specific jurisdictions
Mergers and acquisitions requiring infrastructure integration
AI/ML capabilities available only on specific providers
Geographic distribution beyond single provider footprint
avoid_when: Simple projects where single cloud is sufficient
Data can be hosted in any region without constraints
Strong dependency on single vendor specialized services
Small teams with limited cloud expertise
Lack of maturity for complex distributed operations
component_types: CloudAgnosticAbstraction: Interface that hides provider-specific implementations
ApiGateway: Entry point routing to services regardless of cloud provider
SecretManager: Unified secrets management across providers (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager)
WorkloadScheduler: Intelligent placement and migration of workloads based on capacity, cost, and performance
DataReplicationEngine: Cross-cloud data synchronization with configurable consistency models
GlobalTrafficManager: DNS-based routing with health checks and failover (Cloudflare, Route 53)
UnifiedMonitoring: Centralized observability aggregating metrics, logs, and traces across clouds
IdentityProvider: Centralized authentication federated across cloud boundaries (Okta, Azure AD)
PolicyEnforcementEngine: Cross-cloud policy-as-code (Open Policy Agent, Terraform)
anti_patterns: Distributed monolith with tight coupling across clouds
Shared database accessed from multiple clouds
False portability with cloud-agnostic abstractions for basic services
Cloud-agnostic for everything bypassing beneficial services
Neglecting data gravity with distant compute and data
Split-brain scenarios with both providers accepting writes
best_practices: Establish Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE) for cross-cloud expertise and workload placement decisions
Enforce mandatory consistent tagging (application, environment, owner, cost-center, data-classification) across all clouds
Use Policy-as-Code with Open Policy Agent, Terraform, and provider-specific policies to control resources and prevent shadow IT
Implement Private Connectivity via Megaport, Equinix Fabric, or Cloudflare Magic for cross-cloud networking
Deploy Cloud-Agnostic Databases like CockroachDB, YugabyteDB, or TiDB for distributed SQL across clouds
Centralize Unified Observability with OpenTelemetry and Grafana/Prometheus backends across all providers
Implement Zero-Trust Security with least-privilege access and zero-trust network access (Cloudflare Access, Tailscale, Teleport)
Use Intelligent Traffic Routing with Cloudflare, Route 53, or Cloud Load Balancing with health checks and automated failover
Deploy Cost Intelligence tools like CloudHealth, Apptio, or CloudZero for multi-cloud cost tracking and automation
Follow Phased Migration starting with non-critical workloads, validate, then migrate business-critical applications
